draft.title: Ecumenism and interfaith dialogue
card: Christian churches of different traditions working together. It aims to build co-operation and unity among Christians.
Conversation and joint action between people of different religions, such as Christians, Jews and Muslims. It aims to build understanding and respect, not to merge the religions.
The Uniting Church in Australia was formed in 1977. The Methodist, Presbyterian and Congregational churches joined to create it. It is an example of ecumenism, as all three were Christian.
The two ideas differ in who takes part. Ecumenism happens inside Christianity. Interfaith dialogue crosses the boundary between religions.
draft.remember: Ecumenism is between Christian churches. Interfaith dialogue is between different religions.

a.q: Which activity is an example of ecumenism?
opts: Anglican and Baptist churches hold a joint service
A mosque and a synagogue hold a shared meeting
A church invites a Buddhist temple to a talk
Christians and Hindus hold a shared peace walk
a.why: Anglican and Baptist churches are both Christian, so working together is ecumenism. The other three bring in a different religion, so they are interfaith dialogue.
a.clue: Look for the option where everyone taking part is Christian.

b.q: In Newcastle, a Catholic parish and a Uniting church share a food program. Later, the Catholic parish meets a local Sikh gurdwara to learn about each other's beliefs. How are the two activities best described?
opts: The first is ecumenism and the second is interfaith dialogue
The first is interfaith dialogue and the second is ecumenism
Both are ecumenism because a church takes part in each
Both are interfaith dialogue as each involves cooperation
b.why: Catholic and Uniting churches are both Christian, so working together is ecumenism. A Christian parish meeting a Sikh gurdwara crosses religions, so it is interfaith dialogue. Having a church involved does not make something ecumenical.
b.clue: Ask whether each group in an activity belongs to the same religion.

a.best: Anglican and Baptist churches hold a joint service

b.best: The first is ecumenism and the second is interfaith dialogue

problems.detail: The card says the Methodist, Presbyterian and Congregational churches joined to create the Uniting Church. In 1977 the Methodist Church joined fully, but only part of the Presbyterian Church (about two-thirds) and most Congregational churches joined. A continuing Presbyterian Church of Australia remained. Saying 'most Presbyterian and Congregational congregations' would be accurate.
